newsitem.title: ITALY: EU Dublin summit to issue Mideast plea - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: EU Dublin summit to issue Mideast plea - Chirac.

text.p: France and Italy will ask their EU partners at a summit in Dublin on Saturday to reaffirm Europe's desire to play a role in reviving the Middle East peace process, French President Jacques Chirac said on Friday.

He said the joint approach at the Dublin summit had been agreed at bilateral talks on Friday. "I believe that everyone will agree with it," Chirac told a joint news conference with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was due to meet separately later on Friday with Prodi, in Naples, and with Chirac in Paris to brief them on this week's inconclusive Washington Middle East summit.

The Washington meeting, called by U.S. President Bill Clinton after five days of bloody Israeli-Palestinian clashes, brought together the leaders of Israel, the Palestinian Authority and Jordan but had no European presence.

Chirac said Saturday's statement, to be issued by a special summit called to discuss the EU's workings, should make clear that Europe was making a considerable effort, including financial, to keep the peace process on track.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told Reuters it was important for EU leaders to "give a sense of direction and (express) how they think this process should go".
